$comment: Rotating draft briefs per brand — the seed lane's content plan. `node scripts/social-drafts.mjs seed --auto` picks the week's briefs by ISO-week rotation and files them as SocialDraftRequest asks; the 5-minute drain answers them on the Max pool, and the copy lands in the Hub for a human to stage. Briefs follow the /draft contract: the fact, the audience, the CTA, the hard constraints. Never a metric, customer, price, or date that isn't true — the drafting session will refuse to invent one. Edit freely; rotation is stateless (ISO week % length), so order is cadence. Pillars per brand: content/docs/social/<brand>.mdx.

hogwarts.brief: Feature highlight: online admission — parents apply from their phone, the school tracks every application on one dashboard instead of paper folders. Audience: school owners and administrators in MENA. CTA: book a demo at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: admission dashboard card (template lane, og type). Constraint: no invented numbers — the promise is 'the paper chase ends', not a percentage.

Feature highlight: attendance in one tap — the teacher marks the class in seconds and a parent sees it the same moment. Audience: teachers first, parents second. CTA: see it live at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: classroom lifestyle photo (library: hw-classroom). Constraint: truthful — instant visibility is the feature, don't promise SMS/WhatsApp delivery.

Administrator time-savings: invoices and receipts come out of the system, not out of a spreadsheet — fees, installments, and who-paid-what in one view. Audience: school owners. CTA: https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card with one strong Arabic line. Constraint: no claimed hours-saved figure; 'the end-of-term spreadsheet night' is the pain to name.

MENA education context: hogwarts is Arabic-first and RTL-native — built in Arabic, not translated into it. Menus, report cards, parent messages: all native. Audience: everyone; administrators decide, parents trust. CTA: https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: split card (template lane) — Arabic UI beside English UI. Constraint: keep it proud but calm, no competitor-bashing.

Feature highlight: the timetable builder catches conflicts before the term starts — a teacher can't be in two rooms, a room can't hold two classes. Audience: administrators who build the schedule every term. CTA: book a demo at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card. Constraint: the feature is conflict detection at build time — nothing about AI optimization.

Open-source trust: hogwarts is open source — a school can read exactly how its students' data is handled, and its IT can self-host if policy requires. Audience: school owners and IT decision-makers. CTA: the code and a demo at https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card with the repo motif. Constraint: true today — open source on GitHub; don't promise certifications we don't hold.

Parent visibility: one place where a parent sees attendance, grades, and fees for every child they have in the school. Audience: parents (the B2C trust that closes the B2B sale). CTA: ask your school about hogwarts — https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: lifestyle photo (library: hw-dashboard-device). Constraint: calm reassurance, not surveillance framing.

Feature highlight: exams and grades — marks entered once become report cards, transcripts, and the parent's view without re-typing. Audience: teachers and administrators at term end. CTA: https://ed.databayt.org. Suggested visual: og card. Constraint: the claim is single entry, many outputs — no 'auto-grading' language.
